## Teaching points

1. Document baseline acuity and check for a foreign body, infiltrate or penetrating injury before managing a simple abrasion.
2. Document visual acuity before attributing all blurred vision to a superficial scratch.
3. Look for retained foreign material, infection and penetration; these change the management and referral threshold.
4. Uncomplicated abrasions usually heal quickly. Provide pain relief and a locally appropriate eye-treatment plan with clear review instructions.
